children.text: The Volunteer Management System (VMS) is a centralized web application for managing information on volunteers and volunteer work. The goal is to streamline distribution and simplify finding or requesting volunteer assistance, reducing average assignment times by 30% (down to 4–5 days). Release 1.0 includes senior assistance case intake and tracking, volunteer onboarding, automated background checks (BCS), volunteer assignment, and daily forecasted demand notifications. Release 2.0 adds elementary student tutoring capabilities, Release 2.5 introduces local business sponsor rewards and promotions, and Release 3.0 adds advanced ML forecasting models and native mobile applications. For full release scope details, refer to the Vision and Scope document.

children.text: The Volunteer Management System (VMS) is an entirely new, centralized web application designed to bridge the gap between community members in need (specifically senior citizens and elementary education students) and registered volunteers. It serves as a replacement for the previously fragmented, manual volunteer assignment process. The VMS interfaces directly with external entities, notably the Background Check System (BCS) for security clearances and the Senior People Care Center (SPCC) for over-the-phone intake.

children.text:
The VMS supports multiple direct and indirect user classes: 

  • Senior People (Favored, Direct): Senior citizens living at home who require daily wellness check calls, appointment reminders, and social support. Due to potential technical problems, their profiles are typically created by SPCC employees over the phone. 

  • Volunteers (Favored, Direct): Community members who register to provide support (senior-peers or student-peers). They utilize the application to input their details, select favored activities, and receive matching assignments. 

  • Volunteer Administrators (Favored, Direct): System staff responsible for reviewing newly registered volunteers, managing initial screenings, submitting background checks, verifying educational certificates, and planning weekly allocations using forecasted reports. 

  • SPCC Employees (Favored, Direct): Care center staff who interact with seniors over the phone, record their data, and create or update their profiles within the VMS. 

  • School Administrators (Favored, Indirect / Direct): Educational staff who request volunteer tutors and coaches for young students requiring specialized academic support. 

  • Local Business Sponsors (Favored, Indirect): Local shop owners who offer promotions and incentives to engage volunteers, benefiting from increased downtown business transactions. 

  • Young Students (Dis-favoured / Ignored, Direct): Elementary students receiving tutoring who do not directly log into the system due to parental and security concerns. 

  • General Public / Untracked Citizens (Ignored, Indirect): Citizens are indirectly impacted by reduced crime rates and stronger community cohesion resulting from active volunteer programs.

children.heading: Detailed Use Case Specifications
children.text:
1. Detailed Use Case: Create New Volunteer (UC-02)

  • Use Case ID: UC-02
  • Use Case Name: Create New Volunteer 
  • Primary Person: Volunteer 
  • Secondary Person: None 
  • Trigger: Prospective volunteer accesses the system/application to register. 
  • Preconditions:
    1. The VMS portal is active and accessible online. 
    2. The applicant has not previously registered an active account.
  • Postconditions:
    1. A new volunteer profile is created with status set to Pending Screening.
    2. Profile data is saved in the database for admin review. 
  • Main Success Scenario:
    1. Volunteer opens the VMS registration page. 
    2. System displays the volunteer registration form. 
    3. Volunteer enters personal information (Name, Phone Number, Home Address). 
    4. Volunteer selects preferred volunteer activities (e.g., Senior daily calls, Student tutoring). 
    5. Volunteer uploads supporting documents (if applying for tutoring). 
    6. System validates the submitted data format.
    7. System saves the profile and assigns status Pending Screening.
    8. System displays a confirmation message to the volunteer.
  • Extensions (Alternative Flows):
    • 6a. Incomplete or Invalid Data Input:
      1. System highlights missing or invalid fields (e.g., invalid phone number format).
      2. System prompts the volunteer to re-enter corrected information.
      3. Resume at Step 3.
    • 5a. Volunteer indicates interest in Student Tutoring without uploading proof of education:

System prompts that educational credentials are required for tutoring. 

Volunteer uploads credentials or unchecks student tutoring to proceed.

  • Special Requirements: Must provide a simple user interface to boost user engagement. 

 


2. Detailed Use Case: Approve New Volunteer (UC-06)

  • Use Case ID: UC-05
  • Use Case Name: Approve New Volunteer 
  • Primary Person: Volunteer Administrator 
  • Secondary Person: External Background Check System, Volunteer 
  • Trigger: Admin selects a pending volunteer profile for review. 
  • Preconditions:
    1. The volunteer profile exists in state Pending Screening. 
    2. External Background Check System (BCS) is online and working. 
  • Postconditions:
    1. The volunteer profile status is updated to Approved (or Rejected). 
    2. The volunteer becomes eligible for system matching recommendations. 
  • Main Success Scenario:
    1. Administrator logs into VMS and views pending volunteer profiles. 
    2. Administrator conducts initial screening of profile data. 
    3. Administrator submits profile to the external BCS for police certificate check. 
    4. External BCS processes the check and returns a Passed status within 48 hours. 
    5. (If tutor) Administrator verifies educational credentials. 
    6. Administrator sets volunteer status to Approved. 
    7. System sends approval notification to the volunteer.
  • Extensions:
    • 4a. BCS returns a Failed or flagged check:
      1. System logs police check failure. 
      2. Administrator changes status to Rejected.
      3. System notifies applicant of status determination; process ends.
    • 4b. BCS request submitted outside working hours:

BCS queues request until normal working hours. 

System notifies Administrator that request is queued in external BCS. 

    • 5a. Educational credentials invalid or insufficient:

Administrator marks student tutoring role as rejected. 

Administrator restricts volunteer approval to senior services only. 

  • Special Requirements: Integration with external BCS. 



3. Detailed Use Case: Generate Daily Report (UC-07)

  • Use Case ID: UC-07
  • Use Case Name: Generate Daily Report 
  • Primary Actor: System (Daily Schedule at 06:00 AM) 
  • Secondary Actor(s): Volunteer Admin
  • Trigger: System daily timer triggers a configured schedule, or an Admin requests a report manually.
  • Preconditions:
    1. Historical demand and active senior/student case data exist in the database. 
  • Postconditions:
    1. System generates a daily forecast report for the upcoming week. 
    2. Report is delivered to the Volunteer Admin dashboard/email. 
  • Main Success Scenario:
    1. Scheduled timer triggers system execution at 06:00 AM daily. 
    2. System records active, closed, and pending senior and student cases. 
    3. System runs algorithm to estimate needed cases for the next 7 days. 
    4. System compiles volunteer availability and flags potential incompatibilities. 
    5. System generates the Daily Forecast & Management Report. 
    6. System delivers notification/report to Volunteer Admins. 
  • Extensions (Alternative Flows):
    • 4a. Forecasted demand exceeds available volunteer capacity:
      1. System generates a High Risk Shortage Alert. 
      2. System highlights recommended volunteer re-assignments to severe cases. 
      3. Administrator reviews alert to take manual re-assignment actions. 
  • Special Requirements: Report must complete generation within 60 seconds to prevent administrative delay.

children.heading: Platform and Architecture
children.text:
• A centralized, web-based application accessible to administrators, care center employees, and volunteers via standard modern web browsers.

  • 2-Tier Architecture implemented on the city’s municipal IT infrastructure:


Web Server


  • Operating System: Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9

  • CPU: 4 vCPUs/Cores 

  • Memory (RAM): 16 GB 

  • Storage: 80 GB SSD (primarily for OS, application binaries, logs, and temporary caching).

  • Network: Gigabit interface with static local IP behind a municipal load balancer/reverse proxy (Nginx/Apache).


Database Server


  • Operating System: Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9

  • Database Management System (DBMS): PostgreSQL 15 (robust relational integrity, excellent indexing, and support for external file path references).

  • CPU: 8 vCPUs/Cores (To handle concurrent administrative screening queries, background check status updates, file metadata indexing, and heavy weekly forecasting reports)

  • Memory (RAM): 32 GB ECC RAM (to handle worst-case scenarios in very congested days with multiple requests at the same time)

  • Storage Capacity: 500 GB NVMe SSD (Configured in RAID 10)


Data Architecture Recommendation for Documents:

  • Store the PDF files (educational certificates and background checks) in a secure, encrypted local directory

    • Store file path, metadata, upload timestamp, and verification status inside the PostgreSQL database.

  • Store all other data as tables in PostgreSQL


Backup & Retention Policy:


  • Automated daily incremental backups with weekly full snapshots, routed to a separate municipal backup server to satisfy data retention and integrity rules.

children.heading: Geographical and Organizational Locations
children.text:
• The system operates locally across the city, connecting the municipal administration, the Senior People Care Center (SPCC), local schools, volunteers' homes, and senior residences. 

  • Databases and servers are hosted centrally on the city’s municipal IT infrastructure to manage sensitive records securely across different municipal departments.

children.heading: External Systems and Software Coexistence
children.text:
• Background Check System (BCS): An external automated system that interfaces with the VMS to process criminal background checks. Because it incorporates a mandatory manual review step by police officers, it only processes requests during standard working hours. 

  • Senior People Care Center (SPCC) Telephony/Intake Tools: Internal communications infrastructure used by SPCC employees to converse with senior citizens over the phone while simultaneously recording or updating their data into the VMS.

children.heading: Volume and Scalability Parameters
children.text:
• Designed to handle highly volatile traffic, ranging from a few cases per day up to hundreds or potentially thousands of cases per day during peak loads. 

  • The initial target for the first year is to track 60% of senior cases in the city and provide support to 85% of reported cases, managing an estimated population pool of 10,000 to 15,000 senior cases. 

  • Expected student integration volume is initially forecast at approximately 100 students each semester.

• External System Operational Limits:

    • The Background Check System (BCS) functions strictly during standard working hours due to its reliance on manual police validation steps. The VMS architecture must accommodate queueing and delayed batch processing for background checks submitted outside of these windows. 

  • Government Regulatory and Privacy Policies:

    • Strict governmental regulations mandate that volunteers are legally prohibited from viewing student personal information unless they are officially and securely matched as a "student-peer". 

  • User Accessibility Constraints:

    • Due to technical barriers and isolation concerns, senior citizens cannot conveniently log into the web application directly. Therefore, the system design must accommodate telephone-based intake workflows managed exclusively by SPCC employees on behalf of seniors. 

  • Security and Authentication Restrictions:

    • To protect vulnerable populations (seniors and young children), direct student login is disabled due to parental security concerns, requiring all youth coaching requests to be mediated through school administrators.

  • Municipal Infrastructure & Operating Environment Constraints:

    • The system must be deployed exclusively within the city's municipal IT infrastructure using a 2-tier architecture running Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9 on both the web and database servers.

  • Storage and Document Management Constraints:

    • To prevent relational database bloat and maintain performance, the system must enforce a hybrid storage pattern for compliance records: educational certificates and police background check PDFs must be stored in a secure, encrypted local directory, while file paths, metadata, upload timestamps, and verification statuses are indexed in PostgreSQL 15.

children.heading: Hardware and Infrastructure Assumptions
children.text:
• The municipal IT infrastructure will reliably support the specified RHEL 9 web server configuration (4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM, 80 GB SSD) and database server configuration (8 vCPUs, 32 GB ECC RAM, 500 GB NVMe SSD in RAID 10). 

  • Automated daily incremental backups, weekly full snapshots, and routing to a separate municipal backup server will successfully execute to satisfy data retention and integrity rules.

children.heading: Document and Data Assumptions
children.text: Educational certificates and background check documents received during onboarding will be successfully digitized, processed, and managed via the hybrid file storage and database indexing pattern.

children.heading: Business and Operational Assumptions
children.text:
• The Background Check System (BCS) will be fully developed, tested, and deployed by the municipal government within the designated timeframe (ready by the end of the next month / next few months) and will achieve a processing capability of 1,000 background checks per hour with a 48-hour turnaround time. 

  • Local business owners and downtown merchants will participate as sponsors by offering promotional incentives to volunteers, creating a sustainable motivational loop that supports local economic transactions. 

  • Historical and incoming case data will follow predictable statistical distributions, allowing the VMS analytics engine to accurately forecast weekly case volumes and reduce volunteer assignment time down to 3 days (a 30% reduction from the previous two-week manual average).

children.heading: System Dependencies
children.text:
• Successful and timely volunteer onboarding depends directly on the operational availability, uptime, and processing speed of the external Background Check System (BCS) and police officer verification pipeline. 

  • The VMS depends on the continuous operational staffing of the Senior People Care Center (SPCC) to bridge the digital divide for senior citizens requiring profile creation and daily health tracking.

The Logical Data Model for the Volunteer Management System (VMS) establishes the structural relationships between core data entities required to support senior intake operations, volunteer tracking, automated demand forecasting, background check verification, and downtown sponsor reward redemption.

The data model captures entity attributes, primary keys, and cardinality constraints (one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many relationships) governing system workflows. The complete Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD) and its corresponding symbol notations are provided in Appendix B: Analysis Models of this document.

children.heading: Data Acquisition, Integrity, Retention, and Disposal

children.text:
Volunteer data:

The volunteers data is collected during the volunteers registration into the system. The data will be stored in a centralized database with data accuracy verification systems in place to ensure no fraudulent or fake data is input into the system. The system will regularly make backups of the database incase anything were to happen to the main system. Only the individuals in charge of the system may access the volunteers personal data, except for contact information and the volunteers preferred name when applying for a job. If a volunteer unregisters then the data will stay within the system but display that the individual is not an active volunteer and they will be excluded from any reports.

Client data:

The general client data will be attained the same way as the volunteers, they will include relevant personal information during registration. It will also be stored in a centralized database with data accuracy verification separate from the volunteers database to minimize risk of data loss in case of an incident. Backups will be made regularly, as does the volunteers information database. Client data will be hidden from users and will only be utilized for emergencies or investigation into accidents by administrators. 

 

Job request data:

When a client wishes to request help for a job they will provide the time, location, required manpower, job responsibilities, any required experience or certifications if needed, and any equipment the volunteer must have if necessary. All job request information will be available to users so volunteers can know what the job entails before applying. All data will be kept in its own database with regular backups to ensure secure information.

Sponsor data:

Sponsor data will be input by the company that wishes to partner with the system. Data will include the type of reward, duration of event or promotion, and how long they have been a sponsor for. The types of rewards are coupons, discounts, or other incentives, the event or promotion duration can be fixed if they are in need of volunteers or indefinite if they want to become a long term sponsor. Once a company starts an event or promotion period, the companies contact information, industry/field, locations, biography, and reward type will be available for users to view. Similar to other user data the sponsor data will be in its own database with regular backups to minimize data loss in case of an accident.

children.text: This section defines the external interface requirements for the Volunteer Management System (VMS) across all planned releases (Releases 1.0, 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0), ensuring reliable communication between human user classes, external software services, hardware platforms, and network protocols.

The VMS provides role-based user interfaces tailored to each favored user class (refer to Appendix C: Application Prototype 1 for initial wireframe layouts):

  • UI-01 [Release 1.0] Responsive Web Portal: The primary interface shall be a responsive web application accessible via standard modern desktop and mobile browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) using clean, high-contrast layouts with persistent top-level navigation, role-specific dashboards, standardized form validation messages, and contextual help tooltips.
  • UI-02 [Release 1.0] Volunteer Portal: Shall provide prospective and approved volunteers with a registration wizard (personal info, preferred activities, credential upload), an assignment dashboard displaying matched cases, and an in-app notification center.
  • UI-03 [Release 1.0] SPCC Employee Intake Console: Shall provide a streamlined, single-screen telephone intake form optimized for rapid data entry while conversing with senior citizens over the phone, including case status and urgency indicators.
  • UI-04 [Release 1.0] Volunteer Administrator Dashboard: Shall display pending volunteer screening queues, BCS clearance statuses, candidate matching views (with historical engagement metrics), and the daily 7-day forecast and shortage alert view.
  • UI-05 [Release 2.0] School Administrator Portal: Shall provide a dedicated interface for elementary school staff to submit tutoring requests, specify required academic skills, and view confirmed tutor placements.
  • UI-06 [Release 2.5] Local Business Sponsor Portal: Shall provide downtown merchants with an interface to create, schedule, and manage promotional coupon offers and view verified volunteer engagement summaries.
  • UI-07 [Release 3.0] Native Mobile Applications: Shall introduce native iOS and Android applications enabling volunteers to receive push alerts, view active assignments, and log wellness check-in or tutoring session outcomes on the go.
  • UI-08 [All Releases] Excluded Direct Interfaces: Senior citizens and elementary students shall not have direct login interfaces; all interactions are mediated by SPCC employees and School Administrators respectively.

The VMS interfaces with the following internal and external software components:

  • SI-01 [Release 1.0] PostgreSQL 15 Relational Database Server: Connects via TLS-encrypted TCP/IP (port 5432) on Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9 using logically separated schemas (e.g., core_ops, pii_vault, forecasting) to enforce strict access boundaries while storing entity records and encrypted file URIs.
  • SI-02 [Release 1.0] Encrypted Local Document Store: Interfaces with the RHEL 9 encrypted filesystem directory to read/write uploaded PDF compliance documents (criminal record certificates and educational credentials) referenced by BCS_Record.FilePath.
  • SI-03 [Release 1.0] External Background Check System (BCS): Communicates asynchronously via a RESTful JSON API over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+). VMS submits applicant identity payloads (Volunteer.ID, legal name, birth date, address) and receives clearance outcomes (Passed / Failed) and certificate references within a 48-hour SLA. Requests submitted outside standard police working hours are queued by BCS for next-business-day processing.
  • SI-04 [Release 1.0] Municipal SMTP Email & In-App Notification Service: Interfaces with the city's SMTP relay server to dispatch transactional email alerts (assignment offers, approval decisions, daily 06:00 AM forecast/shortage reports) synchronized with in-app notification records.
  • SI-05 [Release 2.0] Academic Credential Verification Workflow: Rather than an automated external database link, educational credential verification (UC-04) operates as a manual administrative review workflow inside VMS where Volunteer Administrators inspect uploaded PDF transcripts/certificates and record approval status.
  • SI-06 [All Releases] SPCC Telephony Coexistence: No automated CTI/API integration exists with the SPCC phone system; SPCC staff use existing municipal telephones concurrently with the VMS web console.

N/A (No Custom Hardware Interfaces). The VMS is a pure software application deployed on standard municipal virtualized/rack server infrastructure (RHEL 9 web and database nodes) and accessed over standard commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) client devices (desktop PCs, laptops, tablets, and smartphones in Release 3.0). It does not interface with custom sensors, biometric scanners, telephony hardware, or embedded peripherals.

• CI-01 [Release 1.0] Web Transport Security: All browser-to-server and mobile-to-API traffic shall use HTTPS over TLS 1.2 or higher; unencrypted HTTP requests on port 80 shall automatically redirect to port 443.
  • CI-02 [Release 1.0] Data Interchange Formatting: All client-server and external BCS API payloads shall be encoded in UTF-8 JSON; document uploads (background checks, educational credentials) shall be restricted to PDF format (max 10 MB per file).
  • CI-03 [Release 1.0] Notification Delivery Channels: System notifications (assignment dispatches, screening updates, and daily 06:00 AM shortage alerts) shall be delivered dual-channel via authenticated SMTP/TLS email and persistent in-app notification feeds (plus APNs/FCM push notifications in Release 3.0).
  • CI-04 [Release 1.0] Network Isolation: Database traffic between the web tier and PostgreSQL 15 tier shall traverse an isolated municipal VLAN with firewall rules blocking direct external access to port 5432.

• QA-USE-01 [Release 1.0] Learnability & Onboarding Speed: Newly onboarded Volunteer Administrators and SPCC Employees shall be able to complete core workflows (registering a senior case, initiating a background check, or assigning a volunteer) within 15 minutes of initial system exposure without requiring formal classroom training.
  • QA-USE-02 [Release 1.0] Intake Efficiency: An SPCC Employee shall be able to create or update a senior citizen profile and log a support case over the phone in 3 minutes or less, utilizing structured dropdowns and auto-formatted fields (E.164 phone numbers, ISO dates).
  • QA-USE-03 [Release 1.0] Volunteer Registration Simplicity: Prospective volunteers shall be able to complete initial registration and activity selection in under 5 minutes with inline field validation and clear error recovery prompts.
  • QA-USE-04 [Release 1.0] Accessibility: All web interfaces shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA contrast and keyboard-navigation guidelines to support diverse municipal staff and community volunteers.

• QA-PERF-01 [Release 1.0] Interactive Response Time: 95% of standard web UI actions (case lookups, profile creation, volunteer search/filtering, and assignment confirmation) shall complete with a server response time of 2 seconds or less under normal operating loads (up to 100 concurrent users; TBD confirmation with municipal IT).
  • QA-PERF-02 [Release 1.0] Daily Forecast Report Generation: The automated daily 06:00 AM 7-day demand forecast job (UC-07) and shortage alert calculation shall complete execution and dispatch notifications within 60 seconds across a pool of up to 15,000 senior cases and 5,000 volunteers.
  • QA-PERF-03 [Release 1.0] End-to-End Assignment Turnaround: Operational workflow efficiency supported by the VMS matching engine shall reduce average volunteer assignment lead time by 30% from the historical 2-week manual baseline down to 4–5 business days (including the external BCS 48-hour SLA).
  • QA-PERF-04 [Release 1.0] Peak Throughput & Concurrency: The 2-tier RHEL 9 / PostgreSQL 15 architecture shall sustain peak daily traffic spikes of up to 2,000 case transactions per day and 250 concurrent active sessions without HTTP 5xx errors (TBD confirmation).

• QA-SEC-01 [Release 1.0] Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) & Data Isolation: The system shall enforce strict RBAC across logically separated PostgreSQL schemas. Senior citizen and elementary student personally identifiable information (PII—full name, address, phone number, birth date) shall remain hidden from unapproved and unassigned volunteers; an approved volunteer may view contact and case details only for cases explicitly assigned to them.
  • QA-SEC-02 [Release 1.0] Encryption in Transit and at Rest: All external network communications shall use TLS 1.2+. Stored compliance PDFs (police background checks and academic certificates) in the local directory and PII columns in PostgreSQL 15 shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256.
  • QA-SEC-03 [Release 1.0] Authentication & Session Management: All direct users (Volunteers, SPCC Employees, Volunteer Admins, School Admins in 2.0, Sponsors in 2.5) shall authenticate via salted, hashed credentials (bcrypt/Argon2) with automatic session timeout after 30 minutes of inactivity.
  • QA-SEC-04 [Release 1.0] Audit Logging: Every read, create, update, or export operation involving senior PII, student records, or BCS clearance statuses shall record an immutable audit entry (user ID, timestamp, action, target record ID).

While the VMS does not control physical machinery or deliver clinical medical interventions (see Exclusion EX-1), it safeguards vulnerable populations (isolated senior citizens and elementary school children) through mandatory human-safety controls:

  • QA-SAF-01 [Release 1.0] Mandatory Clearance Gate: The system shall strictly prohibit matching or assigning any volunteer to a senior or student case unless their BCS_Record.Status equals Passed and their profile status is Approved.
  • QA-SAF-02 [Release 2.0] Youth Tutoring Credential Gate: The system shall block assignment to any elementary student tutoring case unless a Volunteer Administrator has explicitly verified and approved the volunteer's educational credentials (UC-04) in addition to police clearance.
  • QA-SAF-03 [Release 1.0] Non-Clinical Boundary & Emergency Escalation Notice: The SPCC Intake Console and Volunteer Portal shall display a persistent notice stating that VMS coordinates non-medical wellness checks only and instructing staff/volunteers to contact emergency services (911) immediately if a senior is in acute medical distress.

children.heading: Additional Quality Attributes (Availability, Integrity, and Retention)

children.text:
• QA-AVL-01 [Release 1.0] System Availability: The VMS web portal and database shall maintain 99.5% operational uptime during core municipal operating hours (06:00 AM – 10:00 PM PT, 7 days a week), excluding scheduled maintenance windows (TBD confirmation).
  • QA-INT-01 [Release 1.0] Data Integrity & Post-Assignment Updates: Volunteer engagement metrics and case histories shall automatically update upon completion of each assignment, and database foreign-key constraints shall prevent orphaned cases or unverified assignments.
  • QA-RET-01 [Release 1.0] Two-Year Activity Retention & Archival Policy: Per stakeholder retention rules, the system shall retain active and historical volunteer activity logs and completed case records for a rolling window of 2 years (24 months) for administrative reporting; records exceeding 2 years shall be automatically archived or purged in accordance with municipal privacy policy (TBD confirmation on archival vs. hard deletion).
  • QA-MOD-01 [Releases 1.0–3.0] Modular Extensibility: The backend service layer and database schema shall be modularly decoupled so that Release 2.0 (student tutoring), Release 2.5 (sponsor rewards), and Release 3.0 (ML forecasting and mobile API endpoints) can be deployed without disrupting existing Release 1.0 senior care workflows.

Partially Applicable (Localized for Kamloops, BC, Canada; i18n-Ready Architecture). Because the VMS is deployed exclusively for the City of Kamloops, British Columbia, multi-currency, multi-timezone, and international regulatory variations are N/A. However, the system shall enforce Canadian localization standards and internationalization readiness:

  • I18N-01 [Release 1.0] Primary Language & Future Bilingual Readiness: Release 1.0 shall deliver all UI labels, notifications, and reports in Canadian English (en-CA). All user-facing strings shall be externalized into structured resource bundles (e.g., JSON/i18n translation keys) rather than hardcoded in UI components so that Canadian French (fr-CA) can be added in a future release without code refactoring.
  • I18N-02 [Release 1.0] Canadian Regional Formats: The system shall format telephone numbers using the North American Numbering Plan (+1-XXX-XXX-XXXX), postal codes in Canadian alphanumeric format (A1A 1A1), dates in ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) or standard Canadian format, and scheduled jobs (such as the 06:00 AM daily forecast) in Pacific Time (America/Vancouver, PST/PDT).

The following legal, privacy, backup, and operational requirements apply to the VMS across releases and are not covered under Sections 3–7:

  • OTH-01 [Release 1.0] Municipal & Provincial Privacy Compliance (BC FIPPA): Because the VMS is hosted on municipal IT infrastructure in British Columbia and processes personal data of vulnerable residents (seniors and minors), all data collection, consent notices, and storage practices shall comply with the British Columbia Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA).
  • OTH-02 [Release 1.0] Backup & Disaster Recovery Operations: Automated daily incremental database and encrypted document backups, plus weekly full snapshots, shall execute off-peak and replicate to a separate municipal backup server, supporting a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 24 hours and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 4 hours (TBD confirmation).
  • OTH-03 [Releases 1.0–3.0] Release Migration & Zero-Downtime Cutover: Database schema migrations for Releases 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0 shall include automated rollback scripts and execute during scheduled low-traffic maintenance windows (01:00 AM – 04:00 AM PT) with verified pre-deployment backups.

The following terms, acronyms, and abbreviations are used throughout this SRS:

Term / AcronymDefinition
BCSBackground Check System: The external municipal/government automated police clearance service that processes criminal record checks within a 48-hour turnaround SLA during business hours.
Engagement ScoreA calculated system metric reflecting a volunteer's historical reliability, completed assignments, and commitment level, used by Volunteer Administrators during candidate selection.
ERDEntity-Relationship Diagram: A visual logical data model depicting core VMS entities, attributes, primary keys, and cardinality relationships (see Appendix B).
FIPPAFreedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act: British Columbia provincial legislation governing the collection, protection, and disclosure of personal information by public bodies (including municipalities).
PIIPersonally Identifiable Information: Any data that can identify a specific individual (e.g., full name, home address, phone number, birth date, or police check record).
RBACRole-Based Access Control: A security mechanism restricting system actions and data visibility based on the authenticated user's assigned role (e.g., Volunteer, SPCC Employee, Volunteer Admin).
RHEL 9Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9: The standardized enterprise Linux operating system running on the municipal web and database servers.
Senior-Peer VolunteerAn approved volunteer matched to provide non-medical daily wellness check-in calls, appointment reminders, and social companionship to senior citizens.
SLAService Level Agreement: A formal performance or turnaround commitment between service providers (e.g., BCS 48-hour police check turnaround).
SPCCSenior People Care Center: The municipal care facility whose staff conduct telephone intake with senior citizens and register or update senior profiles and support cases in the VMS.
SRSSoftware Requirements Specification: This document, specifying functional, data, interface, quality, and operational requirements for the VMS.
Student-Peer VolunteerAn approved volunteer who has passed both a criminal background check and educational credential verification (UC-04) to tutor elementary students (introduced in Release 2.0).
VMSVolunteer Management System: The centralized web and mobile software platform specified in this document.
VSDVision and Scope Document: The upstream business requirements document defining project vision, business objectives, release roadmap, and stakeholder profiles.

ERD Symbol Legend & Notation Descriptions

  • Rectangles: Represent system Entities (core data objects/tables within the VMS domain, such as Volunteer, Senior, and Support_Case).

  • Ovals / Ellipses: Represent Attributes (specific properties or data fields describing an entity, such as Name, PhoneNumber, and Address).

    • Underlined or Key Ovals: Indicate the Primary Key (ID) uniquely identifying each entity record.

    • Dashed Ovals: Represent derived, optional, or multi-valued attributes (e.g., Age or isValid).

  • Diamonds: Represent Relationships (association verbs connecting two or more entities, such as Registers / Updates, Assigned, and Submits).

  • Lines with Cardinality Labels (1, N, M): Indicate mapping constraints and participation rules between entities:

    • 1 indicates a Single / One participation constraint (e.g., one Senior is created/updated by an Employee).

    • N / M indicate Many participation constraints (e.g., a Volunteer can be assigned to M support cases, and a Support_Case can involve N entities).
